description: Verified exam notes for 14 November 2026 covering rural housing, India–Egypt trade, tribal development, India–Nepal rail connectivity, Delhi-NCR pollution control, data protection, synchrotron science, Tamil Nadu water governance, narcotics enforcement and preventive health.

stories.title: Five lakh PMAY-G houses announced for eligible families in Odisha
stories.summary: The Union Rural Development Minister announced five lakh pucca houses for eligible poor families in Odisha under Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana-Gramin. The announcement followed a fresh beneficiary survey, and the houses are to be provided in phases; construction was not reported as completed. The Centre and Odisha also plan joint support for rooftop solar on beneficiary houses.
key_facts: The announcement covers 5,00,000 rural pucca houses in Odisha.
Odisha reported 29 lakh Lakhpati Didis against a state target of 27 lakh.
About ₹4,000 crore was announced for Odisha during the year under the Viksit Bharat-G RAM G scheme.
The release said panchayats would receive ₹25 lakh to ₹50 lakh annually; over five years, smaller panchayats could receive up to ₹1 crore and larger ones up to ₹2 crore.
The release also referred to approval of 1,700 km of roads under PMGSY Phase IV.
stories.exam_link: Revise PMAY-G, rural beneficiary identification through deprivation and survey data, Gram Panchayat verification, PMGSY rural connectivity and the Lakhpati Didi initiative linked to self-help groups.
stories.source_title: Ministry of Rural Development: Five lakh PMAY-G houses for Odisha, 14 November 2026

stories.title: Seventh India–Egypt Joint Trade Committee meeting scheduled in Cairo
stories.summary: The Commerce Ministry announced a ministerial visit to Egypt from 15 to 16 November 2026. The programme includes the seventh India–Egypt Joint Trade Committee meeting, a Joint Business Council meeting and a business forum. These engagements were scheduled when the release was issued, not completed outcomes. A delegation of more than 130 business leaders and start-ups is expected to participate.
key_facts: The seventh Joint Trade Committee session is scheduled for 15 November 2026 in Cairo.
The JTC has been elevated to ministerial level.
India–Egypt merchandise trade during April–September 2026 was US$5.04 billion, 64% higher year-on-year.
India exported US$3.87 billion to Egypt and imported US$2.60 billion from Egypt during FY 2025-26.
Planned discussions include market access, pharmaceuticals, engineering goods, renewable energy, green hydrogen, logistics and customs cooperation.
stories.exam_link: Revise Egypt's location linking Africa and Asia, the Suez Canal, India–Egypt Strategic Partnership, bilateral trade mechanisms and the difference between merchandise trade and services trade.
stories.source_title: Ministry of Commerce and Industry: Visit to Egypt and seventh JTC, 14 November 2026

stories.title: Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas programme to cover 246 tribal-development projects
stories.summary: The Prime Minister's Office announced a Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas programme for 15 November 2026, marking the 151st birth anniversary of Bhagwan Birsa Munda. The programme is scheduled to include inauguration or foundation-laying for 246 projects worth about ₹3,000 crore. Because the release preceded the event, the projects are recorded here as planned programme components rather than completed inaugurations.
key_facts: The programme is scheduled at Gadchiroli, Maharashtra, with participation by video conference.
Foundation stones are planned for 19 Eklavya Model Residential Schools.
Foundation stones are planned for 12 Tribal Multipurpose Marketing Centres.
Forty-two other projects are linked to PM-JANMAN and the Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan.
The Ropuiliani Tribal Freedom Fighter Museum in Mizoram is scheduled for inauguration.
stories.exam_link: Revise Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas on 15 November, Bhagwan Birsa Munda, Eklavya Model Residential Schools, PM-JANMAN for Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups and tribal-development institutions.
stories.source_title: Prime Minister's Office: Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas programme, 14 November 2026

stories.title: Indian Railways approves weekly Janakpur Dham–Ayodhya service
stories.summary: Indian Railways approved the introduction of a weekly passenger service between Janakpur Dham in Nepal and Ayodhya Cantt in Uttar Pradesh. The approximately 604-km route is intended to strengthen cross-border mobility and religious tourism between two Ramayana-associated centres. The official release announced approval but did not specify the date on which commercial operations would begin.
key_facts: The service is planned to originate from Janakpur Dham on Saturdays and from Ayodhya Cantt on Mondays.
The route crosses the India–Nepal border through Jaynagar and serves towns in Bihar and Uttar Pradesh.
Commercial stops include Madhubani, Sitamarhi, Raxaul, Narkatiaganj, Gorakhpur, Basti, Mankapur and Ayodhya Dham.
Janakpur Dham is in Nepal, while Ayodhya is in Uttar Pradesh.
stories.exam_link: Revise India–Nepal relations, the open border, Jaynagar's role in cross-border rail connectivity, Bihar and Uttar Pradesh geography, and the cultural diplomacy dimension of the Ramayana circuit.
stories.source_title: Ministry of Railways: Janakpur Dham–Ayodhya weekly service approved, 14 November 2026

stories.title: Delhi-NCR review directs stronger time-bound air-pollution enforcement
stories.summary: The Union Environment Minister reviewed winter air-pollution measures with Delhi, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan and called for coordinated field enforcement. CPCB was directed to seal 191 identified non-conforming polluting industries, while states were asked to complete ANPR-based monitoring. These are enforcement directions and deadlines, not evidence that the region's pollution problem has been resolved.
key_facts: CAQM may initiate criminal prosecution against delinquent transport officials after 30 November 2026 for failure to install required ANPR cameras.
Immediate action was directed at 233 identified traffic-congestion points across NCR.
MCD was asked to complete Multi-Lane Free Flow systems at 154 Delhi border entry points by 31 December 2026.
Dust-generating construction and demolition activities were restricted across NCR from 5 to 20 November 2026.
Of 2,345 targeted industries, 2,298 were connected to Online Continuous Emission Monitoring Systems; the remaining 47 had been closed or sealed.
stories.exam_link: Revise the Commission for Air Quality Management, CPCB, GRAP, Online Continuous Emission Monitoring Systems, ANPR technology and the airshed approach to pollution across state boundaries.
stories.source_title: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change: Delhi-NCR pollution review, 14 November 2026

stories.title: Consent Manager registration framework under DPDP law becomes operational
stories.summary: The registration framework for Consent Managers under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 came into effect on 13 November, and MeitY launched an online registration portal on 14 November. Eligible Indian companies may now apply to become Consent Managers. The framework begins the registration stage; it does not mean every applicant has already been approved or begun providing services.
key_facts: Applications are enabled through the portal dpbi.gov.in.
The minimum net-worth requirement for an applicant is ₹2 crore.
Consent Managers are intended to help Data Principals give, manage, review and withdraw consent through an accessible platform.
The Digital Personal Data Protection Act was enacted in 2023.
stories.exam_link: Revise the DPDP Act, the roles of Data Principal, Data Fiduciary and Consent Manager, lawful consent, withdrawal of consent and the institutional framework for personal-data protection.
stories.source_title: Ministry of Electronics and IT: Consent Manager registration framework, 14 November 2026

stories.category: Science and Technology and International Cooperation
stories.title: India commits over €7 million to Italy's Elettra 2.0 programme
stories.summary: India announced participation as a co-partner in redevelopment of India-centric research beamlines at Elettra Sincrotrone Trieste in Italy. The commitment exceeds €7 million over five years beginning in 2026-27. The investment is for upgraded synchrotron research infrastructure and researcher capacity; it is a future multi-year commitment, not a completed facility upgrade.
key_facts: The existing XRD2 and Xpress beamlines are to be replaced by micro-XRD and Xpress-SB beamlines.
The upgraded facilities will support chemistry, physics, advanced materials and structural biology research.
Indian scientists have used Elettra facilities since 1998.
India is Elettra's second-largest user after Italy, according to the official release.
About 50 to 60 Indian scientists visit Trieste annually for experiments.
stories.exam_link: Revise synchrotron radiation, beamlines, X-ray diffraction, macromolecular crystallography, high-pressure diffraction and science diplomacy in India–Italy relations.
stories.source_title: Ministry of Science and Technology: India joins Elettra 2.0, 14 November 2026

stories.title: First regional conference on Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0 concludes in Tiruchirappalli
stories.summary: The first regional conference on Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0 concluded in Tiruchirappalli, Tamil Nadu, with emphasis on reliable water services, source sustainability and Gram Panchayat-led management. Officials visited Kallanai and rural water infrastructure and participated in Jal Arpan Diwas. The conference described reforms and implementation priorities rather than declaring universal 24×7 supply achieved.
key_facts: Jal Arpan refers to formal handover of drinking-water infrastructure to a Gram Panchayat with continuing technical support.
Women from a Sujalam Shakti Group demonstrated water-quality testing with Field Test Kits at Palamaneri village.
The conference involved seven participating States and Union Territories.
JJM 2.0 emphasises operations and maintenance, water-quality monitoring, source sustainability and capacity building of Village Water and Sanitation Committees.
Five regional conferences are planned ahead of a proposed national review in February 2027.
stories.exam_link: Revise Jal Jeevan Mission, Gram Panchayats, Village Water and Sanitation Committees, Kallanai on the Cauvery, rural water-quality testing and decentralised service delivery.
stories.source_title: Ministry of Jal Shakti: JJM 2.0 regional conference in Tiruchirappalli, 14 November 2026

stories.title: DRI seizes 10.8 kg of amphetamine concealed in an international postal parcel
stories.summary: The Directorate of Revenue Intelligence reported seizure of 10.8 kg of suspected amphetamine from a parcel arriving from Europe at the Foreign Post Office in New Delhi. Eight packets were found concealed within the carton packaging. The substance was seized under the NDPS Act, while investigation into the wider network remained ongoing.
key_facts: The parcel had been declared as containing clothes.
Two concealed pouches were recovered from each of the carton’s four sides.
The recovered pink powder tested positive for amphetamine in the field test described by the release.
DRI functions under the Department of Revenue in the Ministry of Finance.
stories.exam_link: Revise the NDPS Act, 1985, the enforcement role of DRI, customs and postal-channel risks, psychotropic substances and the distinction between seizure, arrest and conviction.
stories.source_title: Directorate of Revenue Intelligence: Amphetamine seizure, 14 November 2026

stories.title: Health Ministry opens preventive-health pavilion at IITF 2026
stories.summary: The Health Ministry inaugurated its pavilion at the 45th India International Trade Fair at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi. The pavilion is open during the fair scheduled from 14 to 27 November and focuses on preventive healthcare, early diagnosis, healthy lifestyles and youth participation. It is a public-awareness and programme-outreach initiative rather than a new healthcare entitlement.
key_facts: The pavilion theme is 'Yuva Bharat, Swasth Bharat'.
Thirty-nine stalls represent 24 national health programmes and organisations.
Activities include CPR demonstrations, health-awareness sessions and a children's zone.
The India International Trade Fair is organised by the India Trade Promotion Organisation.
stories.exam_link: Revise non-communicable disease prevention, early detection, CPR, the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, NITI Aayog, ICMR and the National Health Authority.
stories.source_title: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare: Health Pavilion at IITF 2026, 14 November 2026
